newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Jun gas oil down on prompt sell.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Jun gas oil down on prompt sell.

text.p: Singapore front month June gas oil swaps fell late afternoon on Tuesday on strong selling pressure as players looked to offload amid poor prompt physical demand from regional endusers.
"A lot of sellers emerged this afternoon for June because they feel that there is not much demand for the prompt barrels," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were quoted at $25.00/$25.10 per barrel while July was at $24.95/$25.05, down 20 cents for the front month from Monday's quotes, brokers said.
July was down only 10 cents from Monday leading to a sharp narrowing of the June/July time spread to five cents from a traded 20 cents on Monday.
June gas oil traded earlier in the day at $25.06, 25.05, $25.00 while July traded at $25.00, brokers said. Sellers include a European major, a US major major, and two western traders.
Buyers include a Chinese trader and another European major, traders said.
They said the June market came under selling pressure because of concerns that the market will not be able to absorb all the prompt physical cargoes.
The physical market is in contango with cargoes loading 15 days forward offered at between 10 and 30 cents below those loading 30 days out.

Firmer July prices came despite despite reports of exports of up to 250,000 tonnes of gas oil from the Black Sea and Mediterranean to Asia due to market perception of sustained buying from some traders.
Industry sources said the market is also looking to the re-emergence of enduser buying from China, Indonesia and India for support in July.

China halved its April gas oil imports over March to around 400,000 tonnes and is also said to have bought similar amounts in May and the low purchases are also expected to be extended to June, traders said.
China had reduced its second quarter imports due to high stocks, port congestion and large impors in the first quarter.
Traders said China is likely to raise its imports for July delivery after the high stocks are run down.

Indonesia is expected to raise its imports in July and August due to the scheduled shutdown of a 200,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit at the 265,000-bpd Balikpapan refinery for one month from July 10.
Indonesia has also scheduled to shut down a 100,000-bpd crude unit at its Cilacap refinery for 35 days beginning August 13.
India has raised its July imports to 855,000 tonnes from 315,000 tonnes in June.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted up 50 cents at $101.00/$101.50.
